disclaimer: DEMO medicine list. Doses are copied from public US over-the-counter Drug Facts labels (adults, 12 years and over) and have NOT been approved by a flight surgeon. A real mission replaces this file with the flight surgeons' approved formulary and checklists. Not for real medical use.

allergies.NSAID: Ibuprofen, aspirin or other NSAID pain relievers

conditions.ulcer: Stomach ulcer or stomach bleeding (now or before)

medicines.name: Acetaminophen (paracetamol)
medicines.how: Swallow with a glass of water.

avoidIf.reason: Liver disease: acetaminophen can harm the liver.

interactions.reason: Can change how a blood thinner works: the CMO checks with the flight surgeon.

cautions: Never take it together with another medicine that also contains acetaminophen.
medicines.source: US OTC Drug Facts label, acetaminophen 500 mg (DailyMed)

medicines.name: Ibuprofen
medicines.how: Swallow with water, with food or milk if your stomach is upset.

avoidIf.reason: Stomach ulcer or bleeding: ibuprofen can cause stomach bleeding.
Kidney disease: ibuprofen can harm the kidneys.
Heart disease: ibuprofen can raise the risk of heart problems.
High blood pressure: ibuprofen can raise blood pressure.
Asthma: some people with asthma react to ibuprofen.

interactions.reason: Taken with a blood thinner, ibuprofen raises the risk of bleeding.
Ibuprofen can stop heart aspirin from working and raises the risk of bleeding.
With steroid tablets, the risk of stomach bleeding is higher.
With water pills, ibuprofen is harder on the kidneys.
Another NSAID pain reliever was taken in the last 24 hours.

cautions: Drink plenty of water: in space, dehydration and kidney stones are a risk.
medicines.source: US OTC Drug Facts label, ibuprofen 200 mg (DailyMed)

medicines.name: Meclizine
medicines.how: Swallow with water. To prevent motion sickness, take it 1 hour before the activity.

avoidIf.reason: Glaucoma: this medicine can raise eye pressure.
Emphysema or chronic bronchitis: it can make breathing problems worse.
Trouble urinating: it can make it harder to pass urine.

interactions.reason: With sleeping pills or tranquilizers you will be much more drowsy.
Another drowsy antihistamine was taken in the last 24 hours: more drowsiness.

medicines.source: US OTC Drug Facts label, meclizine HCl 25 mg (DailyMed)

medicines.name: Diphenhydramine

avoidIf.reason: Glaucoma: this medicine can raise eye pressure.
Emphysema or chronic bronchitis: it can make breathing problems worse.
Trouble urinating: it can make it harder to pass urine.

interactions.reason: With sleeping pills or tranquilizers you will be much more drowsy.
Another drowsy antihistamine was taken in the last 24 hours: more drowsiness.

cautions: Do not use it with any other product that contains diphenhydramine, even a skin cream.
medicines.source: US OTC Drug Facts labels, diphenhydramine HCl 25 mg: antihistamine and night-time sleep aid (DailyMed)

medicines.name: Loratadine
medicines.how: Swallow with water. It does not usually make you drowsy.

avoidIf.reason: Liver disease: the flight surgeon may want a different dose.
Kidney disease: the flight surgeon may want a different dose.

medicines.source: US OTC Drug Facts label, loratadine 10 mg (DailyMed)

medicines.name: Oxymetazoline nose spray
medicines.how: Blow your nose gently first. Spray while breathing in through the nose.

avoidIf.reason: Heart disease: decongestants can strain the heart.
High blood pressure: decongestants can raise it.
Thyroid disease: ask the flight surgeon first.
Diabetes: ask the flight surgeon first.
Trouble urinating: it can make it harder to pass urine.

cautions: Use it for 3 days at most: longer use can make the stuffiness worse.
medicines.source: US OTC Drug Facts label, oxymetazoline HCl 0.05% nasal spray (DailyMed)

medicines.name: Polyethylene glycol 3350 (laxative powder)
medicines.perUnit: dissolved in 120–240 mL of water or another drink
medicines.how: Stir the powder into the drink until it dissolves, then drink it all. It can take 1 to 3 days to work.

avoidIf.reason: Kidney disease: ask the flight surgeon before using a laxative.

medicines.source: US OTC Drug Facts label, polyethylene glycol 3350 (DailyMed)

medicines.name: Loperamide
medicines.how: Swallow with water. Keep drinking fluids to replace what you lose.

avoidIf.reason: Liver disease: ask the flight surgeon first.

cautions: Stop and call the CMO if the diarrhoea lasts more than 2 days.
medicines.source: US OTC Drug Facts label, loperamide HCl 2 mg (DailyMed)

medicines.name: Hydrocortisone 1% cream
medicines.perUnit: a thin layer on the itchy skin
medicines.how: Wash and dry the skin, then rub in a thin layer. Wash your hands after.
cautions: Not on broken skin, near the eyes, or on a rash that looks infected.
medicines.source: US OTC Drug Facts label, hydrocortisone 1% cream (DailyMed)

medicines.name: Glucose tablets
medicines.how: Chew them well and swallow. Only if fully awake and able to swallow.
medicines.appearance: white chalky chewable tablets in an orange tube
medicines.source: American Diabetes Association: 15–20 g of fast glucose, recheck after 15 minutes, repeat if still low (the 15-15 rule)

medicines.name: Glucagon emergency kit
medicines.how: Mix the powder with the liquid as the kit shows, then inject into the outer thigh. Turn the person on their side: vomiting is common.
medicines.appearance: orange case with a syringe of liquid and a vial of powder
medicines.source: US drug label, glucagon emergency kit 1 mg (DailyMed)

medicines.name: Aspirin chewable (low-dose)
medicines.how: Chew the tablets, then swallow. Do not swallow them whole.

avoidIf.reason: Stomach ulcer or bleeding: aspirin can cause serious bleeding.

interactions.reason: Already on a blood thinner: aspirin adds a serious risk of bleeding.
Ibuprofen in the last 24 hours can weaken aspirin's effect.

medicines.source: American Heart Association: chew aspirin (162–325 mg) for a suspected heart attack unless allergic or told not to

medicines.name: Epinephrine auto-injector
medicines.how: Pull off the safety cap. Press the tip firmly into the outer thigh (through clothing is fine) until it clicks; hold 3 seconds.
medicines.appearance: pen-shaped auto-injector with a safety cap
cautions: A racing heart, shaking and paleness afterwards are expected.
medicines.source: US drug label, epinephrine auto-injector 0.3 mg (DailyMed)

conditions.title: Headache
conditions.plain: A dull or pressing headache. In space it often comes from fluid moving to the head, poor sleep, too little water or high CO₂ in the cabin.

redFlags.question: Is this the worst headache of your life, or did it start suddenly, like a thunderclap?
Do you have weakness, numbness, trouble speaking, confusion or loss of vision?
Do you have a fever with a stiff neck?
Did it start after you hit your head?

nonDrug: Drink a glass of water.
Check the cabin CO₂ reading.
Rest for 20 minutes in a dim, quiet place.

options.when: Now. If still needed, every 6 hours.
Now. If still needed, every 4 to 6 hours.

conditions.title: Back pain
conditions.plain: Ache or stiffness in the back. Very common in space: the spine stretches without gravity and the back muscles weaken.

redFlags.question: Is there numbness in your groin or legs, or trouble controlling your bladder or bowels?
Did it start after a fall or a hard hit, with severe pain?
Do you also have a fever?

nonDrug: Lie on your back and pull your knees to your chest for 1 minute.
Put a warm pack on the sore area for 15 minutes.
Keep moving gently; avoid lifting heavy loads today.

options.when: Now. If still needed, every 4 to 6 hours.
Now. If still needed, every 6 hours.

conditions.title: Mild fever
conditions.plain: A temperature between 37.5 and 39.4 °C, often with aches or chills.

redFlags.question: Is your temperature 39.5 °C or higher?
Do you have a stiff neck, confusion, or a rash that does not fade when pressed?
Are you short of breath or is your oxygen reading 92% or lower?

nonDrug: Drink extra water.
Rest and stop strenuous tasks.
Keep your distance from the crew and wash your hands often.

options.when: Now. If still needed, every 6 hours.
Now. If still needed, every 4 to 6 hours.

conditions.title: Motion sickness
conditions.plain: Nausea, dizziness or sweating when moving: common in the first days in a new gravity, and in the rover.

redFlags.question: Are you vomiting blood or something that looks like coffee grounds?
Have you been unable to keep any fluid down for more than 12 hours?
Do you also have a severe headache or a hit to the head?

nonDrug: Keep your head still and look at a fixed point.
Take small sips of water.
Avoid reading or screens until it settles.

options.when: Once a day. To prevent it, 1 hour before the activity.

conditions.title: Allergy (sneezing, itchy eyes, mild hives)
conditions.plain: Sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes or a few itchy bumps, for example from dust in the habitat.

redFlags.question: Is your lips, tongue or throat swelling, or is it hard to breathe or swallow?
Do you have hives all over your body and feel dizzy or faint?

nonDrug: Rinse your eyes and face with clean water.
Report dust or a smell in the module to the crew.

options.when: If still needed, every 4 to 6 hours.

conditions.title: Stuffy nose
conditions.plain: A blocked nose. In space fluid moves to the head, so many astronauts feel stuffy for days.

redFlags.question: Do you have a fever above 38.5 °C with pain in your face or teeth?
Is your nose bleeding and not stopping after 15 minutes of pressure?

nonDrug: Sleep with your head raised if you can.
Drink water; dry cabin air makes it worse.

options.when: Every 10 to 12 hours if needed, for 3 days at most.
Once a day, if it comes with sneezing or itchy eyes.

conditions.title: Trouble sleeping (now and then)
conditions.plain: You can't fall asleep or keep waking up. Light, noise, worry and shifted schedules all play a part.

redFlags.question: Are you having thoughts of harming yourself, or feeling hopeless?
Has it lasted more than 2 weeks?
Do you have an EVA, a rover drive or a critical task in the next 8 hours?

nonDrug: Dim the lights and put screens away 30 minutes before bed.
Use the eye mask and ear plugs.
Try the 4-7-8 breathing exercise in Wellness.

options.when: At bedtime, only on nights you need it.

conditions.title: Constipation
conditions.plain: Hard stools or not going for a few days. Common in space with less movement and less water.

redFlags.question: Do you have severe belly pain, a hard swollen belly, or are you vomiting?
Is there blood in your stool?

nonDrug: Drink an extra 500 mL of water today.
Eat fruit, vegetables or other fibre.
Do your exercise session; movement helps.

options.when: Once a day, for 7 days at most.

conditions.title: Diarrhoea
conditions.plain: Loose, watery stools. The main danger is losing too much water.

redFlags.question: Is there blood in your stool, or is it black?
Do you have a fever above 38.5 °C?
Are you very thirsty, dizzy when standing, or not passing urine?

nonDrug: Drink an oral rehydration drink after each loose stool.
Wash your hands well and clean the hygiene area.

options.when: 2 caplets after the first loose stool, then 1 after each further loose stool.

conditions.title: Itchy skin rash
conditions.plain: A small itchy, red patch of skin, for example from dry cabin air or the suit.

redFlags.question: Is your lips, tongue or throat swelling, or is it hard to breathe?
Is the rash spreading fast, blistering or peeling, or do you have a fever?
Is it hot, swollen and painful, or leaking pus?

nonDrug: Keep the skin clean and dry.
Use the skin moisturiser after washing.
Don't scratch; cover it if it rubs on clothes or the suit.

options.when: Up to 4 times a day, for 7 days at most.
Once a day, if the itch is strong.
